name: Ikenna Vasylchuk-Tauiliili
location: Mexicantown Libre, works from a rented corner of his uncle's repair shop, near Ashland and Chicago Ave
description:
Ikenna is seventeen and built like someone who hasn't quite finished deciding how big he's going to be — tall but not yet settled into it, hands that are already large and burn-scarred from glass work, a face that is still soft in the cheeks and absolutely concentrated in the eyes. His skin is a rich dark brown and he keeps his hair in short twists that he occasionally decorates with small glass beads he has blown himself, misshapen and imperfect in ways he considers acceptable. He has a single cosmetic mod — a bioluminescent patch on the back of his right hand in the shape of a solar flare, applied by a friend in exchange for a custom sign, and which he is privately very proud of. He dresses for practicality: heat-resistant gloves hanging from his belt, a work apron scorched in patterns that look almost intentional.

Ikenna learned neon from his uncle, who learned it from a woman who came from somewhere else, and so the craft arrived at him with the character of something that has traveled. He makes signs — functional ones, for the businesses of Mexicantown Libre who can't afford the digital-display minimalism of corporate storefronts — but he also makes pieces he cannot sell and does not try to: suspended glass sculptures that hum at frequencies he calculates by hand, geometric arrangements that change apparent shape as you move around them, portraits of neighborhood figures rendered in colored light. He has a gift he doesn't have language for yet and an ambition he hasn't admitted to anyone.

core_fears: Getting trapped in the repair shop forever, making signs for other people's dreams
Becoming good enough that he stops getting better
core_desires: To make something that people will still be looking at in fifty years
To be taken seriously before he is old enough that it becomes automatic
coping_mechanisms: Work as escape — when things are difficult at home or school he puts more hours in the workshop
Keeps a sketchbook of designs that are too technically ambitious for him yet — the list gets shorter slowly
blind_spots: Dismisses formal arts education as irrelevant to what he does, which is partly protective
Underestimates how much his uncle's shop subsidizes his ability to work — doesn't have a plan for what happens if that changes
psychology.secret: He has been quietly approached by a Palladian talent scout who saw a photo of one of his unsold pieces circulated in an arts feed. He hasn't told his uncle. He hasn't responded. He looks at the message every two or three days.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Casual, streetlevel, Mexicantown Libre inflections; technical only when discussing the craft, at which point he becomes precise and slightly older-sounding
speech_patterns.cadence: Quick when comfortable, halting when discussing things that matter to him — he hasn't learned to be articulate about the work yet
verbal_tics: 'I mean—' (filler when searching for the right word)
'It's not done' (about anything he's made, reflexively)
example_lines: 'It's not like I'm trying to say something. I just — you know when a color sits in a certain shape and it's correct? That's the whole thing.'
'Mr. Olatunde wants his sign in blue-white but I told him it should be amber and he said fine but now I'm not sure I was right and it's been keeping me up.'

story_hooks: One of Ikenna's neighborhood portrait pieces — a suspended glass rendering of a local figure — has been identified by someone with resources as depicting a person who was supposedly dead
The Palladian talent scout's offer comes with terms Ikenna cannot fully read, and he needs someone to explain what he'd be agreeing to
narrative_function: Local color representing the next generation of the city's creative underground; can serve as an unexpected point of access to the Mexicantown Libre community; his artwork sometimes captures or commemorates significant neighborhood events; potential long-arc character who could grow substantially.
augmentations: Single bioluminescent skin patch, back of right hand (solar flare motif); no other mods
daily_life: School in the mornings — he attends, barely, and is passing everything with minimum effort — then straight to the workshop until his uncle closes; late nights he works on his own pieces when the space is empty.
affiliation: Loosely affiliated with his uncle's repair business; no formal arts collective membership

decision_rules: Does not make signs for businesses that have hurt people he knows — there is a short, specific list
Won't rush a piece — has been known to miss a deadline and take the financial hit
escalation_ladder: Walks out of the situation entirely

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Polite, slightly guarded, watches them for a while before deciding
interpersonal_modes.friends: Easy and warm, makes things for people he likes for no reason

stress_responses.low: Works through the night, forgets to eat
stress_responses.medium: Drops school attendance, retreats fully to the workshop
stress_responses.high: Sits in front of an unlit piece of glass for hours without starting — the only time he doesn't work

contradictions: Has enormous pride in his work and almost no ability to accept a compliment — deflects every one as if it were an accusation
habits: Hums without melody while working — a continuous, tuneless sound his uncle has learned to find reassuring
Polishes finished work long after it's done, looking for the thing that's wrong
breaking_points: His uncle's shop closing or the space being taken away
Making something he genuinely loves and having someone reduce it to its monetary value

carried_weapons: Street Custom 'Confession' Modified Industrial Nail Gun
related_entities: Street Custom 'Confession' Modified Industrial Nail Gun

physical_description.build: Tall and still-lengthening, lean with emerging muscularity in shoulders and forearms from glasswork; hands disproportionately large and calloused
physical_description.hair_style: Short twists, occasionally adorned with hand-blown glass beads in mismatched, intentionally imperfect sizes
physical_description.skin_tone: Rich dark brown with warm undertones
physical_description.complexion: Soft cheeks belying concentration in expression; face still carries juvenile roundness but jaw is sharpening. Intense, observant gaze. Minimal facial hair.
distinguishing_marks: Burn scars across both hands and wrists in irregular patterns from repeated glass-working exposure — some linear, some irregular, testimony to years of workshop time
Bioluminescent skin patch on back of right hand shaped like a solar flare — soft blue-white glow, custom commissioned from a friend, source of private pride
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Single bioluminescent patch (solar flare motif) on dorsum of right hand, glowing soft blue-white. No other visible cybernetics; subcutaneous work minimal/absent.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate precision born from glasswork — careful hand placement, economical gestures. Posture slightly forward-leaning as if always mid-concentration. Eyes track details others miss. Still carries teenage awkwardness in limbs he hasn't fully grown into.
physical_description.clothing_style: Strictly utilitarian Tier 2 workshop wear: heat-resistant work apron with visible scorch marks in patterns that read as almost intentional; apron is his de facto signature. Heat-resistant gloves hanging from belt loop. Practical dark pants, worn but clean. No corporate branding. Understated, functional — the aesthetic of someone who has better things to do than fashion, but who owns that fully.

Standing in a neon workshop, surrounded by glass sculptures and colored light tubes. Ashland and Chicago Ave, Mexicantown Libre aesthetic, 2226.
